learningObjectives: Explain what 'automating beyond web applications' means and why a single automation tool needs many engines.
List the technology areas AE1 covers: Excel, PDF, Mail, Windows desktop, mobile, files, and image/AI-based recognition.
Identify the prerequisites and setup needed before starting the course.
Understand how the course is structured and what the Final Exam expects.

elements.description: AS1 and AS2 taught automation of web applications through the XBrowser Engine. But real end-to-end business processes rarely stay inside a browser: an order confirmation arrives as an email, a report is generated as a PDF, reference data lives in an Excel workbook, a back-office step runs in a Windows desktop application, and an approval may happen on a phone. AE1 covers the engines Tosca uses to reach all of those.

Rather than bolting on a separate tool per technology, Tosca exposes each technology through a dedicated Engine that plugs into the shared TBox framework. The way you build a TestCase — Modules, TestSteps, TestStepValues, ActionModes — stays identical whether you are steering a web page, a spreadsheet cell, or a mobile button. That consistency is the point of the framework, and it's what the next module covers.

elements.text: This is a Deep Dive course and part of the Tricentis Tosca On-Prem Product Consultant learning plan. It assumes you already completed the Automation Specialist fundamentals (AS1/AS2) and are comfortable with Modules, TestCases, and ExecutionLists.

bulletPoints: AS1/AS2 = automating the browser. AE1 = automating everything around it.
The TestCase-building workflow does not change per technology — only the Engine behind the Module does.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What you will be able to do

elements.title: Course objectives, grouped by technology
items: Framework — explore the concept of TBox automation frameworks.
Excel — steer and test Excel workbooks and the Excel application, verify cell special properties, compare workbooks, and steer Excel macros.
PDF — scan and test PDF files, create and manage Anchors in the PDF Scan, and compare PDF files using Standard Modules.
Mail — send and receive mails using the Tosca Mail Engine.
Windows desktop — steer and test applications using the UIA and WinX Engines.
Resilience — use the Self-healing property of Tosca.
Files — use Standard Modules to automate file and folder operations.
Hard-to-identify controls — create image-based controls, and install and use Custom controls.
Mobile — create Mobile TestCases using the Tricentis Mobile Agent and Mobile Engine.
Optional — scan Modules using Vision AI.

bulletPoints: Notice the pattern: most lessons are 'here is a technology, here is the Engine that reaches it'. Two lessons (Self-healing, Custom/Image controls) are instead about what to do when identification itself is the problem.

elements.title: Prerequisites
items: Tricentis Tosca installed on your machine, with a valid licence — a training licence can be requested from the Tricentis Support Hub.
The course is primarily based on the Tricentis sample Demo Web shop application (demowebshop.tricentis.com).
Several lessons need local applications available: Microsoft Excel for the Excel Engine lessons, a mail account for the Mail Engine lessons, and a mobile device or emulator for the Mobile lesson.

elements.text: The course was developed on Tosca 16.0. Some screens in the lesson videos will not match a newer Tosca version exactly — the topics and features remain applicable, but expect cosmetic differences in dialogs and ribbon layout, as with any versioned training material.

bulletPoints: Unlike AS1/AS2, several AE1 lessons depend on software outside Tosca (Excel, a mail server, a mobile device). Check you have these before starting the relevant lesson.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Exercise prerequisite: create the AE1 workspace

elements.term: Why a subset is used as a template
elements.description: Each project gets its own Workspace. Subsets are how Tosca artifacts — including the Tricentis Standard Modules — are imported and exported. The course ships a base subset so every learner starts from the same Module set instead of building it up by hand.

elements.title: Setting up the workspace
items: Download the base subset AE1_Base_Subset.tsu from the Downloads section of the Exercise Prerequisites lesson.
Open Tosca Commander and create a new single-user Workspace named 'AE1 Exercises'.
Tick 'Use Workspace template' and select AE1_Base_Subset.tsu as the template, then click OK. The window closes by itself once the Workspace has been created.
Navigate to AE1 Exercises → Modules → Standard modules → TBox XEngines — every engine-specific Standard Module lives here: Excel, Pdf, Mail, Mobile, Vision AI and the rest.

elements.title: What the base subset gives you
items: Modules → Standard modules → TBox XEngines — Excel, Pdf, Mail, Mobile, Vision AI, File, Database, Host, Html, JSON, Java, XML, Sap, Parameter Data.

Modules → Standard modules → TBox Automation Tools — File Operations, Folder Operations, Basic Windows Operations, Buffer Operations, Timing, Process Operations, Expression Evaluation, Numeric Operations, Resource Handling, Selenium.
Empty Module folders to fill as you work: Excel Engine, PDF Engine, UIA Engine, Self Healing, Custom Controls, Image Based Controls.
Modules → Grand Scenario - Demo web shop — pre-scanned Demo Web shop Modules (Login, Navigation elements, Products, Checkout process) for the end-of-course scenario.
TestCases folders mirroring the lessons, plus a Grand Scenario folder with Precondition / Process / Post condition.

elements.text: Notice that the engine lesson folders (Excel Engine, PDF Engine, UIA Engine…) arrive empty. That is deliberate — you populate them by scanning during each lesson. The Standard Modules, by contrast, are supplied ready to use.

bulletPoints: Workspace name: 'AE1 Exercises', created with 'Use Workspace template' + AE1_Base_Subset.tsu.
Engine-specific Standard Modules all live under Standard modules → TBox XEngines.

elements.description: Each lesson pairs a video with one or more hands-on exercises, and most exercises have a solution video showing how it would be completed. The recommended order is: watch the lesson, attempt the exercise yourself, then compare against the solution video.

The Hands-on guides and the Vision AI Theory section are marked optional. The Final Exam draws no questions from optional sections — but Vision AI is still worth understanding, since it is where Tosca's control identification is heading.

elements.text: Every training element in a lesson section (lessons, exercises, notes, knowledge checks) must be completed before the Final Exam unlocks. Some exam questions are exercise-specific, so skipping the hands-on work will leave questions you cannot answer.
Some exercises ship with attached files — download them before starting that exercise. The course also includes Cheat Sheets and Hands-on Use Case material as reference.

bulletPoints: Exercise quizzes do not count towards the final grade; they exist to check comprehension before the exam.
On passing, the Course Completion Certificate appears under your Tricentis Academy Profile.

examPitfalls.title: Skipping exercises and going straight to the exam
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Watching the lesson videos only, then attempting the Final Exam.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The exam contains exercise-specific questions — details you only encounter by actually performing the steps. Complete each exercise before the exam; the section also has to be fully completed before the exam becomes accessible at all.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming the optional sections are examinable
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Spending study time on the Hands-on guides and Vision AI Theory expecting exam questions from them.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The Final Exam does not draw questions from optional sections. Study Vision AI because it is genuinely useful, not because it will be tested.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting the UI to match the videos exactly
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Getting stuck because a dialog looks different from the recording and assuming the step is wrong.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The course was recorded on Tosca 16.0. Features and concepts still apply on current versions; only the visuals shift. Follow the intent of the step rather than pixel-matching the screenshot.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What distinguishes AE1 from the Automation Specialist (AS1/AS2) courses?

options.text: AE1 replaces the TestCase/Module workflow with a scripting language.
AE1 extends automation beyond web applications to Excel, PDF, mail, Windows desktop, mobile, and file operations.
AE1 is about test design rather than automation.

practiceQuiz.hint: The course title is 'Automating beyond web applications'.
practiceQuiz.rationale: AS1/AS2 focus on web automation via the XBrowser Engine. AE1 adds the other engines Tosca uses to reach non-web technologies. The way TestCases are built stays the same — only the Engine behind each Module changes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A learner completes every lesson video but skips the exercises, then tries to open the Final Exam. What happens?

options.text: The exam opens normally and contains only theory questions.
All training elements in a section must be completed before the exam is accessible, and the exam includes exercise-specific questions.
The exam opens but is automatically failed.
Exercises are optional and have no bearing on the exam.

practiceQuiz.hint: The course intro is explicit about what must be completed first.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every training element in a lesson section must be completed before the exam unlocks, and because some questions are exercise-specific, the hands-on work is required to answer them.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which two parts of the AE1 course are marked optional and excluded from the Final Exam?

options.text: The Excel Engine and PDF Engine lessons.
The Hands-on guides and the Vision AI Theory section.
The Mail Engine lesson and the Mobile lesson.
Nothing is optional; every section is examinable.

practiceQuiz.hint: One is supplementary reference material, the other is a forward-looking AI topic.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Hands-on guides and Vision AI Theory are the optional sections, and the Final Exam draws no questions from them. All engine lessons are examinable.
